summary:
Our project, “Abandoned but Not Forgotten: Storytelling About NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars,” is an educational research and presentation project that explores the equipment left behind during NASA's space missions. We developed a visual presentation explaining the history, purpose, and scientific importance of objects such as Apollo lunar equipment, rovers, scientific instruments, Mars landers, and landing components.

The project addresses the challenge of understanding what happens to space equipment after missions are completed. It highlights that these objects are not simply discarded waste but can serve as valuable scientific evidence and historical records. This project is important because it creates awareness about space exploration, technological achievements, environmental responsibility, and the importance of preserving human history beyond Earth. It also encourages students to develop an interest in astronomy, science, and future space research.
details:
Project Overview:

Our project, Abandoned but Not Forgotten, explores the equipment and technology left behind by NASA astronauts and robotic missions on the Moon and Mars. It explains why certain equipment is no longer used, how it was left behind, and how these objects continue to contribute to scientific research and space exploration.

How It Works:

The project uses storytelling, research, images, and presentations to explain the history and purpose of abandoned space equipment. It highlights examples such as Apollo lunar equipment, lunar rovers, scientific instruments, Mars landers, and the parachute and backshell used during the Perseverance rover's landing.

Benefits:

  • Creates awareness about the history of space exploration.
  • Explains the scientific importance of equipment left on other planets and the Moon.
  • Helps students understand NASA missions and space technology.
  • Encourages curiosity about science, engineering, and astronomy.
  • Highlights the importance of preserving historical achievements in space.

Intended Impact:

The main aim is to make people understand that equipment left behind during space missions is not simply waste. Many of these objects have historical, scientific, and educational value. The project encourages interest in future space missions and responsible exploration of other celestial bodies.

Tools and Software Used:

  • Microsoft PowerPoint – to create the project presentation.
  • Internet research – to collect information and reference materials.
  • NASA and NASA/JPL websites – to obtain reliable scientific information and mission details.
  • Images and diagrams – to explain the equipment and space missions visually.

This is a research and presentation-based project; no physical hardware or programming languages were required.

Creativity and Innovation:

The creative aspect of this project is presenting space exploration from a different perspective. Instead of focusing only on successful missions and discoveries, it tells the stories of the objects left behind. It connects science, technology, history, and storytelling to make the topic interesting and easier to understand.

Factors Considered by the Team:

  • Accuracy and reliability of scientific information.
  • Historical importance of the equipment.
  • Scientific purpose and usefulness of abandoned objects.
  • Environmental impact of human activities on the Moon and Mars.
  • Clarity of explanations and visual presentation.
  • Educational value and relevance to future space exploration.
